set.body: Reorganize the project wiki so anyone — a new developer, a PM, an auditor — can find the right page and know whether it is current or historical. Adds a formal content model, stable page identities, truth-state banners, generated navigation and indexes, and an evidence chain from plans to releases. The full design lives in the plan doc; work proceeds in phases, foundations first.

set.body: Extend the item model beyond the fixed core (id/title/status/level/kind/milestone/priority) with a configurable optional-field set, so lightweight and heavyweight processes share one log. Config block (work_item_fields in .work/config.yml) enables fields per team; every enabled field carries a description so humans AND agents use it correctly; disabled fields never appear in prompts, forms, or validation. Recommended default-on: priority, estimate, risk, owner, milestone, acceptance_criteria, labels. Default-off: value, confidence, due_date, severity, time tracking. Dependencies stay typed (blocked_by/blocks, relates_to) and feed the Traceability Index. Design principles: small stable core; explicit documented options; conservative defaults; process-agnostic. set.body: worklog close and worklog update look up the item by exact dict key (fold(...).items.get(a.item) / base(a.item, ...)) instead of resolving prefixes the way worklog reopen already does (id.startswith(a.item)). Passing an 8-char prefix — the normal form worklog show/list output and the docs recommend — silently writes a new orphan phantom item under the short id instead of erroring or resolving to the real item; on update it also skips taxonomy validation since the current-state lookup silently returns {}. Reproduced live: 'worklog close 01KYA8MD' (valid prefix of 01KYA8MDY5HP9MC5KQMJX3BN84) created an orphan closed item instead of closing the real one. Fix: give close/update the same prefix-resolution + not-found error that reopen already has.
set.title: close/update silently corrupt log when given an item-id prefix instead of the full ULID

set.body: sync_dispatch.py's pull step calls the adapter with no --since/--keys when .work/sync-state.json has no 'cursors' entry yet for a repo -- but the adapter's own contract requires one of --since <iso> or --keys, so the very first pull always fails (exit 1: 'pull requires --since <iso> or --keys'). Surfaced during a routine 'worklog sync' run in wiki_ticket_sdd itself -- not specific to any feature, a general first-pull gap. Fix: seed a --since on the first pull (e.g. repo creation date, or the earliest local event timestamp) when no cursor exists yet, instead of calling the adapter with neither.
set.title: worklog sync --pull can never bootstrap: cursor-less pull calls the adapter with no --since, which it requires

set.body: bin/ia_graph.py's build_graph() only creates a 'lands-in' edge when an item sidecar's code entry has a 'pr' key (c.get('pr') is not None) -- a commit-only entry ({'commit': '<sha>'}, written by worklog link-pr --commit with no --pr) creates no edge at all, so trace-check --strict still reports 'no PR/commit link' even after linking a real commit. Hit twice now: v0.13.0's release PR (direct-to-main landings, no PR) and v0.14.0's artifact-pages epic (same pattern -- 11 items linked via --commit, all still flagged). Fix: also create a lands-in edge (to a commit/<sha> node, or similar) when only 'commit' is set.
set.title: ia_graph build_graph() ignores commit-only sidecar code links (lands-in only honors code.pr)

set.body: bin/sync_dispatch.py push_items(): the scope skip ('closed and not ext.get("key") and not forced: continue') is correctly bypassed when --keys forces the item in, but the closed-item branch unconditionally reads ext['key'] (both the dry-run print and the real close() call), assuming a closed item always already has an external key. A closed item that was NEVER pushed (no external.key) and is forced into scope via --keys crashes with KeyError: 'key' instead of create-then-close. Repro: bin/worklog sync --dry-run --keys <ulid-of-closed-never-remote-item>. Hit while reconciling 01KYAH3VHPSEK2RY63J7Y109FR (release item, done, never remote) during v0.14.0 wiki/ticket publish; worked around by manually running the adapter's create step + worklog link before syncing, so the item enters the already-working closed+ext.key path. Fix: in the closed branch, if not ext.get('key'), do create-then-close (mirror the non-closed create path) instead of assuming update-then-close.

set.body: Taking a release snapshot copies the current roadmap file as-is rather than regenerating it from the work log first. If the log has changed since the roadmap was last generated, the release freezes a picture that was already out of date -- and because snapshots are frozen, the wrong picture is permanent. It should either regenerate the roadmap itself, or refuse to run when the roadmap on disk is stale. Two releases in a row have frozen a snapshot missing the release's own work item.

set.body: The generated roadmap only shows an epic when at least one of its children is still open. The moment an epic's last child closes, the epic disappears from the roadmap -- while still counting as open work everywhere else. Finished-but-unclosed epics therefore rot invisibly: one was found open three releases after its last child shipped. The roadmap should surface an epic that has no open children so someone can close it.
set.title: Roadmap hides epics whose children are all closed but which are still open

set.body: Publishing records each page's wiki URL, and the document inventory carries those URLs -- so the index must be rebuilt after publishing, not only before. set.body: Two local work items were allowed to point at the same ticket in the external tracker. Every sync then overwrote that ticket with whichever item changed last, and a cancelled duplicate marked a live high-priority ticket as done. Repairing the ticket by hand did not hold. This work makes a ticket refuse a second owner, adds a way to undo a link, and stops sync from touching any ticket that more than one item claims.
set.title: One local owner per remote ticket (#226)

set.body:

set.body:
Linking an item to a ticket another item already owns is the mistake that causes
the corruption. Refuse it, name the other item and its title so the operator can
see instantly which one is real, and print the two commands that move the ticket
deliberately.
set.title: Refuse a duplicate external key when linking

set.body:
A mistaken link is currently impossible to undo through supported commands, which
is a sharp edge in a log designed so that mistakes are corrected by appending.
The new command retracts the link and warns that the ticket itself may still
carry a marker that has to be cleaned up in the tracker.
set.title: Add a command to undo a link

set.body:
Skip every item in a contested set, print a prominent block naming all claimants
and the exact repair, and exit non-zero so the failure cannot be missed. Healthy
items in the same run still sync.
set.title: Stop sync from pushing a ticket that two items claim

set.body:
The change detection only looks at an item's content, so unlinking or re-pointing
it is silently a no-op and the damaged ticket is never repaired. Record which
ticket was last pushed and treat a change there as a reason to push again.
set.title: Make undoing or moving a link actually re-push

set.body:
Sync records the ticket key right after creating the ticket. If that step can
fail, the run dies with a ticket created but not recorded, and the next run files
a second one. That step must always succeed and never stop the run.
set.title: Keep sync's automatic linking from ever aborting a run
